T1110.name: Brute Force
falsepositives: Users who repeatedly mistype their password
Misconfigured internal health-check or monitoring scripts that authenticate on a schedule

variants.rationale: Broadest possible signal: any authentication failure. Expected to have strong recall but weak precision, since it also catches one-off typos.
Require a burst of >=5 failures from the same source within a 5-minute window, to filter out isolated typos.
Exclude RFC1918 internal source ranges: a misconfigured internal health-check also bursts above the threshold, so the threshold alone isn't enough.
Lower the burst threshold to >=3 to catch the attack earlier in its lifecycle, while keeping the internal exclusion.
Lower the burst threshold further to >=2 to close the remaining recall gap against slow, low-volume brute-force attempts.

T1003.001.name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
falsepositives: EDR/AV engines that scan or reference lsass.exe by name in their own command lines
Legitimate Sysinternals troubleshooting (e.g. Procmon) captured with a filename containing 'lsass'

variants.rationale: Naive single-field keyword match on 'lsass' in the command line. Expected to both miss LOLBin-based dumping techniques that avoid the literal string (e.g. comsvcs.dll MiniDump by PID) and false-positive on benign tools that mention lsass.exe by name.
Replace the keyword guess with named, technique-specific indicators: known dumping tool binaries (procdump, mimikatz) and the comsvcs.dll MiniDump LOLBin technique via rundll32.
